source: reconstruction of Yang, Jia & Yan 2023, Table 2 (example 6)
matched: bi-degree (2,2), polynomial, one Bezier patch each; topology: one closed transversal loop + one isolated tangential point (normals parallel, D has a positive-definite double zero), the point below the loop near the lower tip of the orange; appearance fitted (render_match.py convention): Surfaces-panel camera ortho el=50.00 az=180.00 roll=-1.36, silhouette IoU union 0.7806 / blue 0.6239 / orange 0.4329; result-row camera ortho el=-19.85 az=-5.81 roll=-57.01, mean chamfer 5.72 px to the paper's loop and dot
guessed: construction (orange = bowl + D N, D with the loop/point discriminant) and all coefficients are fitted, not published; the bowl matches the panel's blue crescent, but the orange is only approximate: its upper part rises as two horns (the paper: one pointed tip), the lower lobe is narrower than drawn, and the loop is smooth (the paper's has a pointed top, which a smooth pair of patches cannot produce without a further singular point); in the result-row view the point lies about 4x farther below the loop (relative to the loop's size) than drawn
paper_other_methods: paper: the open-source kernel, the spline library and the commercial kernel returned the loop only (lost the point)
truth_method: closed form: loop = {D = 0} (W from a quadratic in closed form), isolated point = the double zero of D; the blue is a graph along N, so O(u,w) = B(u',w') only for (u',w') = (u,w)
